While you stand still in your calibration pose, small tracker strap slips are slowly absorbed into the current calibration (position only, capped at 5 cm). Large drift is never auto-corrected — recalibrate instead.
Show the per-tracker linking and role-override list. Hide it once your trackers are paired and roled — the tab stays compact for routine use.
Show the fusion tuning sliders. Defaults work for typical hip-belt setups; only flip this on if you understand the tradeoffs.
Per-frame parameters for the midpoint fusion. Defaults work for typical hip-belt setups; tweak only if you understand the tradeoffs.
How aggressively a tracker's confidence drops when its motion spikes above its recent baseline. Higher = a glitch more strongly hands authority to the steady half. Default: 2.
Above this surprise multiplier, the velocity baseline freezes so a sustained glitch doesn't drag the baseline up and stop being detected. Default: 3.
Floor added to the velocity baseline so a frozen tracker doesn't treat any tiny twitch as a giant spike. Default: 0.005 m.
Cap on how far the soft rest-distance pull can drag each tracker. 0 = no pull (raw measurements only), 1 = full rigid solution. Default: 0.3.
Distance error at which the soft pull reaches half its cap. Smaller = tighter rigid behavior; larger = more give for skin/mount flex. Default: 0.05 m.
Distance window inside which the rest-distance baseline is allowed to track changes. Outside it the baseline freezes. Default: 0.05 m.
Smoothing rate for the per-tracker velocity baseline. Higher = faster adaption to motion-pattern changes (more reactive but spikier). Default: 0.1.
Smoothing rate for the inter-tracker rest distance. Default: 0.05.

How quickly the per-tracker confidence weights track current motion surprise. Lower = steadier midpoint with slower glitch recovery; higher = faster reaction but more midpoint motion during normal use. Default: 0.25.
Temporal smoothing for the linked pair's fused rotation. Higher = smoother hips but more rotational lag; lower = snappier when the two trackers flex apart. 0 = no smoothing. Default: 0.08 s.

Multiplies the size of every body-part accept zone used when matching trackers to roles during full-body calibration. Higher = more forgiving of unusual body proportions, high-mounted trackers, a wide stance, or an imperfect T-pose, at the cost of occasional mis-assignment. Default: 1.

Stretches and collapses the avatar's arm, leg and spine bones so its proportions match your own, instead of relying on one uniform scale. Arms are fitted from your arm span; legs and spine need a hips tracker. Your standing height is preserved exactly, so this never moves your feet off the floor. Other players see the avatar at its authored proportions.
Resizes individual bones at calibration so your hands and hips land where the avatar's are. Recalibrate after changing this.
How far a bone may stretch or collapse from its authored length. Higher values fit your body more exactly but alter the character's proportions more visibly. 0 disables the fit.
Distributes wrist and elbow roll along optional twist bones to prevent the mesh from pinching at the wrist when the hand rotates. No effect on rigs without twist bones.
How evenly the forearm twist bone spreads the wrist's roll along the bone. 1 = even gradient (no wrist pinch); 0 = off. Default: 1.0
How evenly the upper arm twist bone spreads the elbow's roll along the bone. 1 = even gradient; 0 = off. Default: 1.0

With a head and hips tracker, gently scales the avatar's spine so its torso length matches yours. Stops a mismatched avatar spine from crumpling (avatar torso too long) or over-stretching (too short). Measured once at calibration; only you see the change.
Uniformly stretches or shrinks the avatar's spine a small amount so it spans your real head-to-hips distance. Does nothing without a hips tracker, or when the avatar already matches you.
The largest length change allowed, as a fraction (0.12 = up to 12% longer or shorter). Bigger corrects larger mismatches but can visibly change your torso length. Default: 0.12
IK refinements modeled on real biomechanics.
Routes spine twist preferentially to the upper chest (thoracic) since the lumbar is biomechanically twist-resistant. Cuts spine yaw weight, boosts upper chest yaw.
Counter-yaws shoulders past 30° of chest twist, mimicking the way the scapula slides on the rib cage during torso turns.
Adds a small forward pitch to the neck so the head sits more naturally forward of the neck axis.
Forces hip-to-chest twist to distribute 75% upper chest / 25% spine — the real anatomical ratio for axial rotation.
Holds each spine bone inside the range of motion of the real vertebrae it stands for — the lumbar barely twists, the chest barely folds, the neck is free. Stops impossible spine poses.

Places the chest at its own target instead of leaving it wherever the head solve happens to put it, so the torso follows your real chest (or a chest tracker) more faithfully. The head stays exactly on the headset.
Damps the leg's roll about the hip-to-foot axis so a still, near-straight standing leg doesn't twist with tracking jitter. Real turning still tracks without lag.

Bends the knee in the plane your lower-leg tracker is actually facing instead of a fixed body-relative guess, so the knee stops snapping backward and follows your leg as you turn it. Also drops an old upward nudge on the chest so the spine follows your real chest position. Off restores the previous forward-pole behavior.
Master switch for hip / chest / foot / knee trackers. Turning this off immediately drops back to head + hands + foot IK. Re-enable and re-calibrate to use trackers again.
Open Sound Control input on UDP 9000 / 9001 for face tracking and avatar parameters from external programs (VRCFT, etc).
Drive your avatar's facial blendshapes from face tracking data. Diagnostics for the active state are shown on the My Avatar tab.
Drive your avatar's eye bones from eye tracking data. The natural eye look keeps running when disabled.
Enables procedural foot placement when standing still without foot trackers.
Suppresses jump and landing animations and the landing hip dip while full-body trackers are calibrated.
Enables virtual capsule collision between elbows and chest to prevent arm clipping through the body.
Pushes elbows outward when they penetrate the chest capsule.
Allow body collision to push the elbow even when an elbow tracker is driving it. Off lets the tracker fully control a tracked elbow.
Adds weight to the predicted elbow so waving your hands does not throw it around.

Only applies when you have no elbow tracker. Lags the predicted elbow slightly, the way a real forearm's weight does, so fast hand motion does not swing it. An elbow tracker is your own input and is never lagged.
Lower is heavier drag. 1 Hz is very heavy, 8 Hz is barely noticeable.
Corner frequency of the elbow drag, in Hz. Lower values damp waving harder but make the elbow trail further behind a deliberate reach. Default 2.5.
Enables the hand collision capsule for IK solving.
Radius of the virtual chest capsule used for elbow collision. Default: 0.18
Extra buffer padding around the chest capsule. Default: 0.02
Radius of the virtual hand target capsule. Default: 0.05
Extra buffer around hand capsule. Default: 0.01
Raises and protracts shoulders based on hand target position before arm IK runs.
Detects a shrug from the hands or elbow trackers while your arms hang at your sides and raises the shoulders to match. Default: on
How much the shoulder raises when the hand is above it. Default: 0.4
How much the shoulder moves forward when the hand reaches out. Default: 0.3
Maximum bend angle for the spine chain. Default: 90
Arm extension ratio where struggle blending begins. Default: 0.9
Arm extension ratio where struggle is fully applied. Default: 1.0
Maximum rotation delta allowed for the chest bone per frame. Default: 90
Maximum rotation delta allowed for the hip bone per frame. Default: 90
Fraction of forward/back lean absorbed by the spine bone (lumbar). Default: 0.45
Fraction of head-twist absorbed by the spine bone. Lumbar twists very little. Default: 0.10
Fraction of side-lean absorbed by the spine bone. Default: 0.35
Fraction of forward/back lean absorbed by the upper chest (thoracic). Default: 0.25
Fraction of head-twist absorbed by the upper chest. Default: 0.30
Fraction of side-lean absorbed by the upper chest. Default: 0.20
Scales bend weights with head-to-hips compression: spine folds more when crouched, straightens when reaching up. 0 disables. Default: 0.5
Maximum forward bend per spine joint contribution. Default: 60
Maximum backward bend per spine joint contribution. Default: 25
Maximum side-bend per spine joint contribution. Default: 25
Caps how far the neck bends away from the chest before the chest and spine take over, preventing neck overbend. Default: 45
Forward lean angle past which the pelvis tilts forward to share the bend. Default: 30
Maximum additional pelvis pitch contributed by the hinge. Default: 15
Shifts the hips back as the head drops, so a squat or forward bow sits over the feet instead of folding straight down. Multiplies the head's drop distance; 0 disables. Default: 1

Moves the hips back as your trunk folds forward, the way a real body counterweights a bend to keep its balance over the feet. Without it the whole fold happens around a pinned pelvis and the chest drives down into the body. Multiplies how far your neck travels forward; 0 disables. Default: 0.38
Caps how fast the elbow can swing around the shoulder-to-hand axis, so collision pushes and pose flips ease in instead of popping. Lower = smoother (more lag); 0 disables. Default: 720
Spring frequency for the body's lag behind head motion. 0 disables. Default: 12
Damping ratio. 1 = critically damped (no overshoot). Default: 1.0
Under-relaxation for the spine CCD aim. Lower = smoother but softer reach; 1 = full step. Default: 0.8
Axial twist the lower back (lumbar) may use to reach an off-center head. A real lumbar barely twists — lower bends sideways instead of corkscrewing. Default: 0.25
Axial twist the neck (cervical) may use; the joints between interpolate. Higher lets the neck turn freely like a real spine. Default: 0.9
How much the chest yaws to follow hand targets when no chest tracker is present. 0 disables. Default: 0.3
Cap on the chest yaw contributed by arm-swing. Default: 15
Feeds head linear velocity into the chest spring so the body leads quick head moves instead of just lagging. 0 disables (pure reactive spring). Default: 0.7

Extra cervical bend at full head-down on top of the 5° base. 0 = constant 5° lordosis; positive scales with how far the head is looking down. Only used when Cervical Lordosis (Anatomy) is on. Default: 8
Forward cervical bend held in a neutral, level-head pose, before pitch coupling is added. Only used when Cervical Lordosis (Anatomy) is on. Default: 5
Fraction of the lordosis bend applied at the neck rather than the upperChest, when an upperChest bone exists. 1 = all neck. Default: 0.65
Clamp on head pitch up/down before the lordosis solve, so a steeply pitched head can't drive the neck past anatomical limits. Default: 80
Head pitch magnitude at which the extreme-look response (extra spine roll plus hips/chest shift) begins ramping in. Default: 50
Head pitch magnitude at which the extreme-look response reaches full strength. Should sit above the onset value. Default: 80
Maximum extra spine roll added at full extreme look-down. Default: 10
Maximum extra spine roll added at full extreme look-up. Default: 4
Maximum horizontal hips counter-shift at full extreme look, in meters. Default: 0.025
Maximum horizontal chest counter-shift at full extreme look, in meters. Default: 0.04
Maximum downward hips shift at full look-down, in meters. Default: 0.015
Maximum downward chest shift at full look-down, in meters. Default: 0.025
Downward hips shift at full look-up, in meters; much smaller than the look-down drop. Default: 0.0005
Downward chest shift at full look-up, in meters; much smaller than the look-down drop. Default: 0.001
Synthesized chest/spine motion when no tracker drives the torso. Per-axis cascade fractions, resting S-curve bias, and hips yaw deadband.
Fraction of head pitch (look-up/down) absorbed by the synthesized chest. 0 = chest stays vertical; 1 = chest matches head pitch. Default: 0.30
Fraction of head tilt (side bend) absorbed by the chest. Default: 0.30
Fraction of head pitch absorbed by the synthesized spine (lower in the chain, so usually less than chest). Default: 0.10
Fraction of head tilt absorbed by the spine. Default: 0.10
Pushes the resting chest position forward of the neck-hips line, giving the chain a natural kyphosis. Scaled by avatar height. Default: 0.025
Hips ignore head yaw changes smaller than this many degrees, suppressing HMD micro-jitter. 0 disables. Default: 4
Slew rate for the synthesized neck rotation toward the head. Higher = snappier, lower = more smoothing. Default: 40
Slew rate for the synthesized chest rotation. Default: 25
Slew rate for the synthesized spine rotation. Default: 30
Slew rate for the synthesized hips yaw. Lower values reduce hips snap on quick head turns. Default: 20
Small forward offset (in meters at default avatar scale) so hips don't sit perfectly under the neck — gives a subtle pelvic tilt. Default: 0.02

Degrees the head can turn before the chest/spine/hips start following. The torso holds inside this cone, then catches up to the head; the cone re-centers when the head stops, so reversing must re-cross it. 0 = follow immediately. Default: 45
How quickly the torso eases into and out of following once the head crosses the play cone. Lower = softer, slower blend (removes the click at the edge); higher = snappier. Default: 8

When off, the torso follows your head immediately in VR (no yaw play), so the head can't turn independently of the chest. Enable to use the Torso Yaw Play cone in VR too. Desktop always uses the configured play. Default: off
Global multiplier for all smoothing filters. 1x = default. Higher values greatly increase smoothing but add latency. WARNING: Values above 10x may cause noticeable input delay.
Global position smoothing frequency. Lower Hz increases smoothing and latency. Higher Hz feels more immediate but may jitter.
Global rotation smoothing frequency. Lower Hz reduces micro-wobble but adds delay. Higher Hz feels snappier but may shimmer.
Controls smoothing strength when movement is very small. Higher values make the avatar steadier when still, but slower to start moving.
Controls how aggressively smoothing is reduced during fast motion. Higher values reduce lag during quick movement, but may reintroduce jitter.
Controls how much motion speed affects smoothing behavior. Lower values are steadier; higher values feel more responsive but noisier.

Temporarily ignores every performance limit for this session only. Resets on relaunch — never saved to disc. Useful when you want to see a specific avatar at its full fidelity without editing your saved caps.

Opt-in filters applied to remote avatars as they load. Trim limits destroy excess extras (animators, lights, particles, trails, lines, cloth, jiggle rigs, unity colliders) so the avatar still renders. Hard-block limits (triangles, bounds, texture memory, material slots, bones, skinned/basic meshes) fall back to the loading mesh instead — meshes aren't trimmed because deleting one usually destroys the body or head. Sensible defaults are on; raise or disable any limit below.
Raw polygon and skeleton counts from the asset bundle header.

Desktop only. Your head pivots at the base of your neck, not at itself, so looking down carries your eyes forward - out over your feet. In VR the headset does this on its own because it physically rides that same lever arm. Desktop used to pin the camera above the hips, so the gaze tipped, the chest hunched to follow, and the head never actually went anywhere.
Carry the head when looking up/down
Moves the camera forward as you look down and back as you look up, by the amount your avatar's own neck geometry says it should. Turn this off to pin the camera over the hips as it was before.
1.0 is the full swing implied by your avatar's neck-to-eye distance. Lower it if the camera travel feels like too much; 0 disables the carry entirely.

How far the camera pulls back when you look UP, as a fraction of the look-down carry. Looking up is not the mirror of looking down - your upper back takes most of it, so your skull does not slide backward nearly as far. 1.0 would treat them the same.
